about: Party of each non-governor statewide executive officeholder as of January 2026, and whether the general election carries party labels. Verified on 2026-10-13 against live Wikipedia pages: lieutenant governor, attorney general, secretary of state, treasurer, auditor, comptroller or controller (where listed there) and agriculture commissioner rows for the 50 states. Verified rows cite the Wikipedia source and carry no estimated flag; partisan-ballot status was taken from each page's elected-office listing. Superintendent, insurance, labor and land commissioner, mine inspector, utility and railroad commission, board, mayor, D.C. and territory rows, and the Arizona and New Jersey lieutenant governor rows, could not be checked against a live source (Ballotpedia, NASS and per-office pages failed or returned nothing) and carry an estimated note. Joint-ticket lieutenant governors are marked partisan. On 2026-10-23 the 60 rows not checked on 2026-10-13 were each checked against a fetched page (sourceId checked-2026-10-23, with the page and a quote on the row); their party is the holder's on the opening day, January 20, 2025, and each row also names the holder on January 1, 2026.

lieutenant-governor.quote: Arizona is holding its first election for lieutenant governor in 2026 ... scheduled to take office on January 4, 2027. Until that date, the office is empty.
lieutenant-governor.note: No officeholder on either date, so null party is right. But the office is filled by a partisan joint-ticket general election (2026 ballot: "Andy Biggs (R) / Sine Kerr (R)", "Katie Hobbs (D) / John Giles (No party preference)"), so partisanElection should be true, not false.

state-board-of-education-president.quote: In 2025, these testimonies were delivered by State Board President Jacque Patterson on behalf of the State Board
state-board-of-education-president.note: Members are nonpartisan (https://ballotpedia.org/District_of_Columbia_State_Board_of_Education: "Office Type: Nonpartisan"; "Jacque Patterson | Nonpartisan | January 2, 2021"). The board elects its president "at its first public meeting each calendar year" (https://sboe.dc.gov/node/1639091), so Patterson was still the 2025 president on January 1, 2026, and https://sboe.dc.gov/node/1565381 lists "Jacque Patterson President, At-Large". The exact January 2025 meeting date was not found, so opening day could fall just before his election.

board-of-education.note: Repo records null party and nonpartisan. The official 2024 Election System summary prints party labels on board candidates (St. Thomas/St. John: "DEM Kyza A. Callwood, PhD", "REP Sophia del Rosario"). Members and parties come from Wikipedia as a fallback (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Islands_Department_of_Education); every start date there is January 6, 2025 or earlier, so 7 D and 2 I on both dates. Conflict: that Wikipedia page says "Elections are formally nonpartisan", while the official summary prints the labels. The owner or lead should decide which one the game follows.

Sablan (R)". Mendiola (R) was elevated July 24, 2025 after Gov. Arnold Palacios died and Apatang became governor (https://ballotpedia.org/Dennis_C._Mendiola). Infobox "Office Type: Partisan", and the results carry party labels, so partisanElection should be true. January 2026 party matches the repo (Republican); opening-day party and the partisan flag do not.
